cards.front: Recall a key point about Environmental Geology
cards.back: Contaminated land: former industrial sites with polluted soil and groundwater; requires remediation before redevelopment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Environmental Geology
cards.back: Landfill: waste disposal in quarries; liner systems prevent leachate contaminating groundwater; methane is captured or flared

cards.front: Recall a key point about Environmental Geology
cards.back: Geothermal energy: heat from Earth's interior used for electricity and heating; clean, renewable but location-dependent

cards.front: Recall a key point about Environmental Geology
cards.back: Carbon capture and storage (CCS): injecting CO2 into deep porous rocks to reduce atmospheric emissions

cards.front: Recall a key point about Environmental Geology
cards.back: Sustainable resource use: recycling, reducing consumption, finding substitutes for scarce minerals

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — environmental geology?
cards.back: 1. For Environmental Geology questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. When interpreting data, consider the quality and limitations of the evidence 4. Apply your understanding of Environmental Geology to fieldwork observations and map data 5. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
